studies.label: Phase 2: randomized constructive-comment writing experiment

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 410:2), Introduction, Phase 2 description
counts_source.quote: with a different set of 103 Indian and American crowd workers on Prolific.

arms.name: HAI-written comments (test)
arms.description: Writers drafted comments and used GPT-4 to rewrite them through supplied or custom prompts. They could accept, edit, reject, or regenerate suggestions before submitting their final comments. Every writer was required to request a suggestion. PDF pp. 10-11 (printed pp. 410:10-410:11), Section 3.2.

arms.name: Human-written comments (control)
arms.description: Writers produced constructive comments independently, without external assistance such as the Internet or ChatGPT. PDF p. 10 (printed p. 410:10), Section 3.2.

studies.task: Write constructive English comments expressing personal views in response to a homophobic thread and an Islamophobic thread relevant to the writer’s country.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 410:10), Section 3.2, Writing Task; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 410:11), Figure 2 and live rewriting prompt; model release year and exact snapshot are not stated

preregistration.where: No preregistration or explicitly designated primary outcome is identified in the full paper or Appendix A.

estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Semantic similarity of comments by different writers sharing a thread and stance. Methods name the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence transformer for draft-final similarity (PDF p. 12, printed p. 410:12); the cross-writer analysis does not independently restate the model (PDF p. 17, printed p. 410:17, Section 4.2.3).

sources.locator: PDF p. 18 (printed p. 410:18), Table 8, Semantic similarity row; columns Human-written comments (control), HAI-written comments (test)

estimates.notes: Compared across different writers within the same arm, thread, and stance. The paper does not establish pair enumeration, aggregation, the independent observation unit, or analysis-specific writer counts. Unit and counts therefore remain null; no participant-level SD, SE, or CI is printed. Table 8 prints a dash in the statistics column. The text reports no significant difference but does not print an exact p-value or numeric test statistic. Higher raw scores mean more similarity.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Separate Prolific raters chose the more constructive member of a same-thread, same-stance HAI-versus-Human comment pair. The reported arm level is the percentage of pair evaluations selecting HAI, not an independent mean creativity rating. Multiple chi-square tests used Bonferroni corrections. PDF p. 12 (printed p. 410:12), Section 3.2; PDF pp. 14-15 (printed pp. 410:14-410:15), Section 4.2.1.

sources.locator: PDF p. 15 (printed p. 410:15), Section 4.2.1, Human Evaluation of Constructiveness; test also in Table 6, HAI vs. Human, Both demographic
sources.quote: significantly more constructive than human-written comments in 64% of cases, with small effect size (𝜒2(1, 𝑁= 802) = 62.56, 𝑝< 0.000005,𝜙= 0.28, odds ratio=3.19).

sources.locator: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 410:14), Section 4.2.1, Human Evaluation of Constructiveness
sources.quote: which included 401 pairs of HAI vs. Human comments

estimates.notes: The observation count is pair evaluations, not unique text pairs or writers. Higher preference means better rated constructiveness (output quality), not an explicit creativity score. The prose also prints chi-square N=802 and phi=0.28; neither is treated as a writer count or a second independent contrast. The relation between the printed chi-square denominator and pair evaluations is not explained, so se_basis is unclear. No adjustment for repeated comments, writers, or raters is stated. The control preference share is shown only in Figure 4, so it is not transcribed or inferred as a complement. The paper’s odds ratio is transcribed without recalculation.

estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Cosine similarity of comments by different writers sharing a thread and stance. Methods name scikit-learn CountVectorizer for draft-final similarity (PDF p. 12, printed p. 410:12); the cross-writer analysis does not independently restate the implementation (PDF p. 17, printed p. 410:17, Section 4.2.3). This is word-count similarity, not semantic embeddings.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Word count, as specified in Table 3. Methods: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 410:9), Table 3, and PDF p. 12 (printed p. 410:12), Quantitative Analysis. Full-sample comment-level comparisons: PDF p. 32 (printed p. 410:32), Table 15.

sources.locator: PDF p. 32 (printed p. 410:32), Appendix A, Table 15, Length row, HAI vs. Human column

estimates.notes: Table 15 prints a dash for this full-sample HAI-versus-Human contrast. No numeric test, exact p-value, full-sample arm mean, SD, SE, or CI is supplied. Figure 5 shows the distributions and unlabelled averages only; no value is read from the plot. Table 19 supplies country-specific means, which are not pooled or substituted. estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: SMOG index computed with the Python textstat library (Table 3). The paper interprets a higher index as better wording and sentence structure. The listed measure categories do not directly fit this readability formula; it is not a human rating or a creativity-scoring model. Methods: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 410:9), Table 3, and PDF p. 12 (printed p. 410:12), Quantitative Analysis. Full-sample comment-level comparisons: PDF p. 32 (printed p. 410:32), Table 15.

sources.locator: PDF p. 32 (printed p. 410:32), Appendix A, Table 15, Readability score row, HAI vs. Human column
sources.quote: Readability score U=7843, Z=8.64, p<0.000001, r=0.63

estimates.notes: The same cell prints Z=8.64. Higher_is other denotes a higher SMOG index; the paper interprets it as greater readability and better wording, but it is not a creativity rating. The usefulness construct follows the reconciled form. No full-sample arm means or SDs are printed in text or tables; the averages appear only as unlabelled points in Figure 5 and are not digitized. Table 19 contains country-specific means, which are not averaged or substituted. The test operates on comments without a reported adjustment for repeated comments from each randomized writer; participant-level precision is unavailable. The paper does not state the standardizer of r.

open_items: The study prints the overall analyzed writer count, but the randomized total, per-arm people counts, and outcome-specific analyzed people counts are not printed. Recruitment and completion counts differ; the reason and timing of the discrepancy are unstated. Do not derive writer counts by dividing the arm-specific comment counts. See PDF p. 2 (printed p. 410:2) and PDF p. 12 (printed p. 410:12), Table 5 and Participant Recruitment.

Cross-writer similarity needs the observation unit, pair enumeration, aggregation, participant links, and dependence handling. No participant-level SD, SE, or CI is supplied. Exact nonsignificant tests for cosine and semantic similarity are omitted. PDF pp. 17-19 (printed pp. 410:17-410:19), Section 4.2.3 and Table 8.

Distinct-2 and type-token ratio need definitions and clarification of within-comment versus across-comment computation. Their independent observation units and counts are not stated, so across-person diversity cannot be confirmed. PDF pp. 18-19 (printed pp. 410:18-410:19), Table 8 and accompanying text.

The constructiveness preference analysis needs its contingency-table construction, analysis-specific writer/rater counts, and precision accounting for repeated outputs and evaluations. The reported chi-square denominator and pair-evaluation count are not the same, and the stated evaluations-per-rater procedure does not explain the total. PDF pp. 12 and 14-15 (printed pp. 410:12 and 410:14-410:15), Human Evaluation of Constructiveness and Table 6.

Full-sample linguistic-feature arm means and SDs are absent from the tables/text. Figure 5 contains unlabelled points and Table 19 contains country-specific means only. The nonsignificant Table 15 contrasts have no printed test statistic or exact p-value. Participant-level precision for the comment-level analyses is not supplied. PDF p. 16 (printed p. 410:16), Figure 5; PDF pp. 32-33 (printed pp. 410:32-410:33), Tables 15 and 19.

No exact GPT-4 snapshot, model release year, preregistration, or study-specific public data/code release is identified in the saved paper. The generic software and model links are not a release of this experiment’s data.

The excluded incorporation subset has an unresolved people-versus-comments label, and the excluded opinion-distortion description has an unresolved denominator. Neither can provide a verified people count for the randomized contrasts. PDF pp. 16 and 19 (printed pp. 410:16 and 410:19).

Readability uses the SMOG index, with higher values interpreted by the authors as better readability. Its constructiveness interpretation is not an explicit creativity judgment; the supplied measure categories do not directly fit this index. PDF p. 9 (printed p. 410:9), Table 3, and PDF p. 16 (printed p. 410:16), Section 4.2.1.
Equivalence of the saved arXiv manuscript and the later publisher version identified in the citation record is not established by this extraction.
The standardizer of the reported rank-test effect r is not stated. No SE or confidence interval for r is printed. PDF p. 18 (printed p. 410:18), Table 8; PDF p. 32 (printed p. 410:32), Table 15.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-11 against the saved arXiv v5 PDF. Read the complete markdown conversion in consecutive chunks, including references and Appendix A. Extracted the text of every cited PDF page with PyMuPDF and recovered Tables 8 and 15 with find_tables(). The later publisher version identified in the citation record was not used. Only the randomized writing experiment S4 is retained; its screening identifiers and arm names are preserved. Independently checked all agreed counts, question, construct, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai, and within_person fields against the paper. The overall writer total is directly printed on PDF p. 2; recruitment, completion, and comment counts on PDF p. 12 do not establish randomized or analysis-specific arm people counts. Individual assignment is between subjects (PDF p. 10, Section 3.2), so every estimate has within_person null; repeated comments and randomized thread order do not make this a randomized-order AI crossover. AI remains available while test-arm final comments are produced (PDF p. 11), so outcome_with_ai is true and no after_ai outcome is extracted. Semantic similarity, cosine similarity, and ROUGE-L explicitly compare different writers on the same thread and stance (PDF pp. 17-19); they retain across_people/diversity/more_similar, with null statistical units because aggregation is unspecified. Distinct-2 and TTR retain with_ai/other/other and null units because vocabulary variety within a comment cannot be distinguished from diversity across people. Constructiveness is output quality, coded usefulness, with higher preference denoting more_creative in the codebook vocabulary; this is not an explicit originality rating. The rated-pair count is not a count of writers or unique text pairs. Its unexplained chi-square denominator leaves se_basis unclear. Linguistic features are comment-level outputs; readability uncertainty does not account for repeated comments from each writer. Word count is elaboration with the positive length direction. Other linguistic counts are ancillary text features with higher_is other. SMOG is retained as the paper’s readability/quality proxy under usefulness, with higher_is other and a documented null measure because the supplied measure vocabulary has no matching readability-index category. The current codebook’s length and text_features codes are used where the screening form predates those additions. All eligible full-sample contrasts of S4-O1 through S4-O12 are represented, including separate cosine/ROUGE-L and distinct-2/TTR records. S4-O13 and S4-O14, the other study phases, all within-arm and editing analyses, model-only comparisons, subgroup results, self-reports, and effects adjusted for post-treatment length are accounted for in not_extracted. No additional eligible full-sample outcome or contrast was found. The diff has no estimates unique to either extractor. Canonical slugs follow A, including length and readability, whose B aliases denote the same contrasts. Figure-only values and country means are not digitized, converted, or averaged. All retained numbers agree with the PDF; no effect, uncertainty, missing count, or arm level was computed. Dashes are not zeros or exact p-values. Source quotations retain printed trailing zeros and signs; JSON numeric serialization may omit trailing zeros. Additional Z statistics and phi remain in notes or the source quotations because the schema has one test and one paper_effect object per contrast. Source fields reference the corresponding stats objects once and omit unsupported null values; empty fields lists document table dashes. Evaluators are distinct from writers, and their HAI-versus-Human judgments are recorded once under S4. No cross-paper participant reuse is stated.
